metrics.rationale: User requests '尽可能透过 255–280 nm 的太阳盲紫外信号' (maximize transmission of 255-280 nm solar-blind UV signal). This is the detector's passband.
User requests '尽可能抑制 300–700 nm 可见光背景' (suppress 300-700 nm visible background). Maximizing reflectance in this stopband minimizes transmitted background.
User requests '尽可能抑制 700–1100 nm 近红外杂散光' (suppress 700-1100 nm near-infrared stray light). This is the second rejection band requiring high reflectance.

standard.metric_rationale: Three metrics cover all three wavelength bands explicitly named in the request: one passband (255-280 nm) where transmission must be maximized, and two stopbands (300-700 nm visible, 700-1100 nm NIR) where reflection must be maximized to suppress unwanted light. I chose mean_transmittance for the passband because the user says '透过' (transmit), and reflectance_stopband for the rejection bands because the catalog recommends this name 'for a rejection or stopband requirement' and maximizing reflectance directly achieves the stated goal of '抑制' (suppress). I deliberately omit absorption/emissivity metrics because the request focuses on transmission and background suppression, not thermal properties. I use band-mean rather than worst-case because the user says '尽可能' (as much as possible) without specifying that every single wavelength point must meet a threshold, and mean metrics provide smoother optimization gradients for multilayer design.
standard.formula_rationale: This arrangement treats the UV signal throughput and the suppression of visible and infrared background noise as equally critical contributions to the detector's performance. Since the user requested maximizing transmission in the passband while simultaneously maximizing reflectance in both stopbands without specifying a hierarchy among these goals, each metric contributes equally to the final score. Direct addition ensures that a design achieving high performance in all three spectral regions ranks higher than one that excels in only one, reflecting the concurrent priority of signal collection and background rejection.
